# MCP server guide

`genefox mcp` serves GeneFox's analyses to an MCP client over stdio. Each tool runs the same
analysis code a GeneFox app screen runs, and returns that screen's numbers as JSON. Most tools
also write a PNG figure and can write the screen's CSV, a GeneFox recipe, or a single-figure
HTML document.

See [Install & resources](install.md) and the [CLI reference](cli.md).

## Starting the server

```bash
genefox mcp --resources /path/to/Resources --output-dir ~/genefox-out
```

`genefox mcp` never prints the CLI's update notice and never checks for updates; update an
installer install with [`genefox update`](cli.md#genefox-update-check-version-xyz) from a terminal.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--resources <dir>` | A copy of the app's scientific resources directory; or `GENEFOX_RESOURCES`, then `<resolved executable directory>/../share/genefox/Resources`, then `<X>.app/Contents/Resources` for a `Contents/Helpers/genefox` or `Contents/MacOS/genefox` executable, then a source checkout's the app's scientific resources directory for a binary under its `.build` folder. Automatic roots require `ScientificResources.json`; every source uses the same integrity checks. With no folder, a missing one, or one without `ScientificResources.json`, the server does not start (status 78, the reason on stderr). If its digests or the gene reference then fail the background check, gene tools answer `resource_unavailable` naming the reason, and no figure is drawn. |
| `--cache-dir <dir>` | Download cache; or `GENEFOX_CACHE_DIR`. Default `~/Library/Caches/GeneFoxCLI` on macOS, `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/GeneFoxCLI` (or `~/.cache/GeneFoxCLI`) on Linux. Mount a persistent volume in containers; on WSL prefer the Linux filesystem. |
| `--output-dir <dir>` | Where figures, CSVs, recipes and HTML are written; or set `GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR`. Default `<system temp>/genefox-mcp`. Files are only ever created there, never overwritten. |
| `--enable-legacy-tools` | Also list the five [legacy tools](#legacy-tools), which take local paths or URLs. |
| `--imported-store <dir>` | The imported-dataset store the legacy `render_recipe` may read. A tool argument cannot name a store. |
| `--allow-root <dir>` | An extra local read root for the legacy `validate_recipe`/`render_recipe` paths, repeatable; or `GENEFOX_MCP_ALLOWED_ROOTS` (path-separated). The output directory and the imported store are always roots; a model-named path outside every root is refused. |
| `--warm <list>` | Prefetch `toil`, `pancan` and/or project ids such as `TCGA-BRCA`, in the background. |
| `--call-timeout <seconds>` | One deadline (1–3600 s) for every call, replacing each tool's own. |
| `--help`, `-h` | Print the usage and exit 0. |
| `--max-concurrent-calls <n>` | How many `tools/call`s run at once (1–64; default half the processors, 2 to 4). Up to 16 more queue; beyond that a call answers `rate_limited`. See [Limits](#limits-deadlines-and-cancellation). |

An option error exits with status 64, and a missing resources folder with status 78, before the
server reads any input. Otherwise the server
prints one self-check line to stderr and then serves until stdin closes, for example:

```
genefox mcp: pid=152 resources=/path/to/Resources (flag) inventory=available reference=available font=ok pin=ok cache=/home/user/.cache/GeneFoxCLI out=/tmp/gfout allowlist=on legacy=off deadline=per-tool calls=4 queue=16 entitlement=free(not-linked) flavor=release version=1.1.0+unknown
```

Some fields in that line need explanation:

- **`allowlist=on`**: in `mcp` mode the network transport admits only an exact list of
  public-data hosts, over HTTPS on port 443, and re-checks every redirect. PedcBioPortal, loopback and GeneFox's own cloud hosts are
  deliberately absent.
- **`entitlement=free(not-linked)`**: see [Entitlements](#entitlements-genefox-pro).

**Progress.** A `tools/call` whose request carries `params._meta.progressToken` gets a
`notifications/progress` every 10 seconds until it answers, with the seconds elapsed as
`progress` (no `total`: a call cannot know its own length), so a client that resets its timeout
on progress keeps waiting through a slow first call. Without a token nothing is sent; each slow
tool's description gives its expected time.

Stdout carries only protocol messages. Logs, including one
`genefox mcp: host_not_allowed …` line per refused request, go to stderr.

## Connecting a client

Every client starts the server the same way: it runs the command
`genefox mcp [options]` and talks to it over stdin and stdout. Use absolute paths, because a
client may start the server from any working directory.

Long calls need a long client timeout. The server's own deadlines are 300 s, or 900 s for
the slow tools (see [Limits](#limits-deadlines-and-cancellation)), and a cold first call can
take minutes. Several clients stop waiting sooner than that by default; each client section
below says how to raise its limit.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport stdio genefox --scope user \
  --env GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR=$HOME/genefox-out \
  -- /usr/local/bin/genefox mcp --resources /path/to/Resources
```

Or commit a project-scoped `.mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "genefox": {
      "command": "/usr/local/bin/genefox",
      "args": ["mcp", "--resources", "/path/to/Resources"],
      "env": { "GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR": "/Users/you/genefox-out" }
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code reads these timeout settings, all in milliseconds:

- **`MCP_TIMEOUT`** limits server startup.
- **`MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`**, or a per-server `"timeout"` in `.mcp.json`, limits a single tool
  call.

Check the Claude Code MCP documentation for the current defaults.

### Claude Desktop

Claude Desktop uses the same `mcpServers` shape, in `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "genefox": {
      "command": "/usr/local/bin/genefox",
      "args": ["mcp", "--resources", "/path/to/Resources", "--output-dir", "/Users/you/genefox-out"]
    }
  }
}
```

I could not verify the file's location or Claude Desktop's tool-call timeout here; check
Claude Desktop's documentation for both.

### Codex

```bash
codex mcp add genefox --env GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR=$HOME/genefox-out \
  -- /usr/local/bin/genefox mcp --resources /path/to/Resources
```

Or in `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.genefox]
command = "/usr/local/bin/genefox"
args = ["mcp", "--resources", "/path/to/Resources"]
env = { GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR = "/Users/you/genefox-out" }
startup_timeout_sec = 30
tool_timeout_sec = 960
```

Codex documents defaults of `startup_timeout_sec = 10` and `tool_timeout_sec = 60`. A
60-second tool timeout ends most cold GeneFox calls early, so raise it as shown. Check
Codex's documentation for the current keys.

### OpenCode

In `opencode.json` (or `opencode.jsonc`):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "genefox": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["/usr/local/bin/genefox", "mcp", "--resources", "/path/to/Resources"],
      "environment": { "GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR": "/Users/you/genefox-out" },
      "enabled": true,
      "timeout": 960000
    }
  }
}
```

OpenCode's per-server `timeout` is in milliseconds; its documented default is 5000. In
OpenCode 1.18.34 it bounds every request to the server, tool calls included, not only the
tool listing: a 75-second call is cut off at `"timeout": 60000` with
`MCP error -32001: Request timed out`, and completes at `"timeout": 960000`
. Set it to 960000 so the 900 s
tools can finish.

## Protocol surface

The server speaks protocol version `2024-11-05` and reports the server as
`genefox` version `1.1.0`. Each line on stdin is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, and each response
is one line on stdout. The server handles these messages:

| Message | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `initialize` | Returns `capabilities: {tools: {}}`, `serverInfo` and `instructions`: the usage rules a model should follow, which summarise this guide. |
| `ping` | Returns `{}`. |
| `tools/list` | The tools this process may offer (see [Entitlements](#entitlements-genefox-pro) and [Legacy tools](#legacy-tools)). The list and the dispatcher read the same registry, so a listed tool is always callable. |
| `tools/call` | Runs a tool. Its result is one `text` content item holding the tool's JSON. `isError: true` means the tool ran and reports a [tool error](#tool-errors). |
| `notifications/cancelled` | Cancels the call named by `requestId`. The cancelled call writes no response. |
| any other id-less message | Silence. |
| any other method | JSON-RPC error `-32601`. |

## Tool catalogue

See the generated [tool catalogue](tools.md).

## Argument conventions

TCGA/GDC human gene inputs use GeneFox's existing approved-symbol and curated-alias
reference: for example, `Her2` resolves to `ERBB2` and `PD-L1` to `CD274`. An approved
symbol takes precedence over an alias. Imported feature IDs and GEO probes retain
their literal spelling and organism-specific meaning.

Cohort expression, gene signatures, heatmaps and differential panels return
`data.gene_resolution`: the original token, canonical symbol, exact dataset field,
dataset version, mapping release and source checksums. GDC STAR expression uses
the verified annotation declared by the dataset sidecar. A custom loader's unknown
mapping source is represented as `null`. Provider-supplied dataset versions use the
bounded `untrusted_dataset_version` key; reports and CSV retain the complete version.
With `csv: true`, these tools also write
`gene_resolution_csv`; the primary data CSV keeps its existing columns. Captured
reports retain the mapping provenance, and saved views retain the requested tokens.


`gene_info` accepts a symbol or a quoted Entrez ID and supports human genes only.
A numeric ID must match the final human record exactly; a different or redirected
record is refused as `gene_identity_mismatch`. A genuine missing record is
`gene_not_found`; malformed or incomplete upstream metadata is `upstream_malformed`.
The returned symbol is NCBI's official name, while summary and aliases remain
under `untrusted_*` keys.

Every tool reads its `arguments` under these rules:

- **Closed schemas.** Every input schema has `additionalProperties: false`. An unknown key is
  refused with `invalid_argument`, naming the key in `field`, so a misspelt key is reported
  instead of silently changing the analysis.
- **`null` means absent.** For an optional field, an empty string (after trimming) also
  counts as absent.
- **Types.** A wrong JSON type is refused with a sentence such as
  `gene: expected a string, got a number.` JSON `true` decodes as a boolean, not as the
  number 1.
- **Strings** are trimmed, then checked against a maximum length and, where the tool has
  one, a whole-string pattern. A TCGA gene symbol must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9.-]*$`,
  with at most 30 characters, and is upper-cased as the TCGA screens do. The GTEx gene is
  trimmed but not upper-cased, as that screen does.
- **Enumerations** must be one of the listed values. A project id is matched
  case-insensitively and answered in canonical form (`tcga-stad` becomes `TCGA-STAD`).
- **Integers and numbers** are checked as doubles before any conversion. A value must be
  finite and within the schema's `minimum`/`maximum`, and an integer must also be whole.
  A value out of range is refused, never clamped.
- **String lists** are trimmed and de-duplicated case-insensitively. A list over its maximum
  count is refused, never truncated.
- **Figure size.** A tool with a `size` argument also accepts `width_in`, `height_in`,
  `dpi` (72–1,200) and the figure-style keys (`survival_detail`, `show_row_counts`,
  `show_caption_color_keys`, `show_figure_legends`). A custom size must stay within the
  app's side limits, 8,192 px per side and 16 megapixels in total. `dpi` is accepted only
  together with `width_in` and `height_in`.
- **Figure file name.** A tool with a `size` argument also accepts `output_name`, a stem for
  the figure's file name in place of the tool name and the title's slug. It takes letters,
  digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starts with a letter or digit, and is at most 64 characters. A
  name with a separator (`/`, `\`, `:`), a `..`, or any other character is refused before the
  tool runs. Only the figure's descriptive part changes; see [Figures](#figures).
- **A heatmap opened from a differential-expression result** (`from_differential_expression`) records its comparison and `top_n` in its `deep_link` and recipe (`de:` and
  `de_top:` flags). `open_destination` and a recipe replay reopen it as one: the comparison is
  rerun and its top genes taken again over its samples under the DE group strip, as the apps reopen it; a recipe flag this build cannot read runs nothing. A comparison by molecular
  subtype does not draw the default Subtype strip beside the DE group strip that already shows it.
- **Figure axes (GeneFox Pro).** The tools whose figures have continuous axes also accept
  `x_min`, `x_max`, `x_scale`, `y_min`, `y_max`, `y_scale`, `value_min`, `value_max` and
  `value_scale`, each tool only for the axes its
  figures have: `x` and `y` for a scatter or volcano (`geo_gene_correlation`,
  `tcga_top_correlates`, `geo_top_correlates`, `tcga_differential_expression`, and the PC1 x PC2
  scatter of `tcga_sample_pca` and `geo_sample_pca`, which refuse a customization with
  `biplot`, `scree` or `correlated_genes`, whose figures have no customizable axis), `value` for
  a box, violin or strip (`tcga_tumor_normal`, `tcga_pan_cancer_expression`,
  `tcga_compare_cohorts`, `reference_treehouse_expression`, `gtex_tissue_expression`,
  `cbioportal_expression`), and the axes of whichever figure `figure_kind` or the grouping draws
  (`tcga_expression`: all three; `tcga_gene_signature`: `x` for the histogram, `value` for the
  grouped box; `geo_series_expression`: `x` for the ungrouped histogram, `value` for a one-factor
  box, violin or strip (`tcga_expression`'s `ecdf` has no customizable axes), `x` and `y` for a continuous characteristic's scatter, none for a two-factor
  view; without `geometry` a `value` key means the box and an `x` or `y` key the scatter, and a
  characteristic the matrix shows to be the other kind is refused once it is read). A bound is a finite number in data units on either scale; a scale is `linear`
  (the default) or `log10`. A histogram's x bounds restrict its binning range. Values outside a
  bound, and values at or below zero on a log axis, are not drawn; the figure says how many in
  its caption and its description. A reversed range, a non-positive bound on a log axis, an
  axis the figure does not have, or a figure kind with no customizable axis (a survival curve,
  a two-factor box, an ECDF) is refused with `invalid_argument`. Every one of these keys
  is Pro (`publicationStudio`) and refused with `entitlement_required` unless the server's
  context grants that capability (see Entitlements). A customization is saved with what the
  call writes: a recipe records it as one `axes:` flag on its destination
  (the same keys, `axes:value_min=7;value_max=12;value_scale=linear`) and in its presentation
  metadata, whose Methods line names the axes; `open_destination` and `genefox render` pass a
  recorded flag back to the tool, so a replay draws the same axes and stays Pro-gated, and a
  flag this build cannot read runs nothing. A CSV is the data, unchanged (`csv.customization`
  and `csv.customization_note` say so); an HTML document embeds the customized engine figure
  (`html.parity: app_document_engine_figure`); `figure: false` returns the data and echoes
  `customization` with a `customization_note`. Significance brackets on a customized value axis test the values it
  shows, on its scale, as ggplot2 does. A caption that cannot fit, or would squeeze the plot, is
  refused with the size that would work; it is never cropped. A drawn customized figure reports
  `figure.customization` (the value's stable JSON) and `parity: engine_only`. `genefox render`
  takes the same values as `--x-min`, `--x-scale` and so on, for an imported plot or signature
  replay and for a signature's `--r-script` (`x` for the score histogram, `value` for the
  one-factor box plot). The script draws them as GeneFox does: values outside a bound, and
  values at or below zero on a log axis, are removed before anything is binned or summarized,
  which is ggplot2's scale-limits behaviour (`scale_x_continuous(limits = )`,
  `scale_x_log10()`), not `coord_cartesian()`'s zoom; the already-filtered geometry is drawn
  with `oob = scales::oob_keep` and the figure's caption. A public recipe replays the axes it
  recorded, and refuses the flags.

Every refusal is a tool error whose `code` is `invalid_argument` and whose `field` names the
argument. It happens before any network request.
No argument of a non-legacy tool is a filesystem path or a URL to fetch. `open_destination`
takes a `genefox://` link, which it decodes as the app's route planner does; it does not
fetch it.

## Results and the `untrusted_*` trust model

A successful result is a JSON object. Analysis tools return `tool`, `data`, `display` (the
screen's sentences and tables, to quote verbatim), `caveats` and `provenance`. `provenance`
holds `sources`, `genefox_cli` (the version), `transport: "live"` (or `"record"` / `"replay"`), `fetched_at` and, where a
screen applies, `parity_screen`.

When a result list is capped, `truncated` discloses its `field`, `kept` and `total` counts.
One capped list produces an object; multiple capped lists produce an array of those objects,
so every cap is disclosed.

**Third-party text is never placed under a plain key.** Text that comes from a dataset, a
portal or a model goes under a key named `untrusted_*`. Examples
are GEO sample characteristics and author labels, CSV headers named after them, Reference and
cBioPortal labels and study text, local-model replies, and a deep link that carries GEO text
(`untrusted_deep_link`). The `initialize` instructions tell the model to treat these fields
as data, never as instructions. Each string is capped at **120 characters**, with a trailing
`…` when cut. A few diagnostic fields use their own larger caps; for example, GEO
supplementary refusal diagnostics allow 512 characters for a file name and 1,200 for a
reason. When a file name is derived from GEO text, the written path is returned as
`untrusted_path` / `untrusted_file_name`.

## Figures

TCGA and GEO expression offer a cumulative distribution (`geometry=ecdf`) over the
retained observations, including constant-valued samples. GEO distribution exports
retain grouping controls and apply any `keep_groups` subset before pooling values. It uses the same
GeneFox engine as the cards on the apps. Its export recipe preserves the ECDF
selection. ECDF axes are fixed; custom bounds or scales refuse before loading data.

Expression distributions offer box, strip and violin plots, with histogram or ECDF where
that screen's schema offers them. The expression bar option is retired. For one release,
MCP accepts the older `bar` and `median_bar` spellings as box-plot aliases and returns a
migration caveat. Saved views, links and recipes that recorded a bar also open as a box
plot with a notice; `genefox render` writes the notice to stderr. Keep the returned caveat
with the figure. Genuine count, proportion and ranked bar charts retain their own geometry.

A figure tool draws through GeneFox's shared engine and writes its figure create-only under the output
directory. The optional `format` argument picks the file: `png` (the default, a raster), `svg`
(vector, with editable text) or `tiff` (raster, the extension `.tif`). Every figure is written in
all three formats from the same drawing, and `format` follows the file's extension and media type
(`format` and `mime_type` in the result). SVG keeps the figure's labels as editable text. It then
returns `figure` with these keys:

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `path`, `file_name`, `bytes`, `sha256`, `width_px`, `height_px` | The file written. For a PNG the pixel size is read from the file itself. |
| `format`, `mime_type` | The file's format (`png`, `svg` or `tiff`) and its media type. |
| `geometry`, `size` | What was drawn. `size` is the preset token, or `custom`. |
| `description` | The engine's description of the figure. |
| `alt_text` | Alt text: the engine's own summary and caveat if it has one, otherwise the description, otherwise a sentence built from the title. |
| `data_table` | `[{label, value}]`, one row per drawn element (group, arm, legend row, or point), in drawn order. |
| `data_table_rows`, `data_table_truncated`, `data_table_note` | The table's row count before the cap; whether the table was cut; and, only when it was, a sentence saying so. |
| `data_table_unavailable` | Replaces the table when the engine attached no element description. |
| `parity`, `parity_screen`, `parity_note` | See [Parity tokens](#parity-tokens). |

**File names.** A figure's file name is

```
<NN>_<tool>_<slug>_<W>x<H>in[_<dpi>dpi].<ext>
```

- `NN` is the figure's number in this server session, counted from 01 and never reused, so two
  figures from one session never share a name, even when they come from the same tool.
- `tool` is the tool that drew the figure, and `slug` is the title's slug. `output_name`, when
  given, replaces `tool_slug` and nothing else.
- `W` and `H` are the size in inches, to one decimal; `dpi` is the resolution. A vector file
  (`svg`) has no resolution, so its name has no `_<dpi>dpi`.
- `ext` is the one extension the format takes: `png`, `svg` or `tif`.

Example: `01_tcga_pan_cancer_expression_box-plot_7.2x6.0in_300dpi.png`.

A name that is already taken is never replaced. The file takes `-2`, `-3` and so on before its
extension, so `01_..._300dpi-2.png` is the second file with that name.

The data table is capped at **200 rows**. Only
scatter and volcano figures, which have one row per point, reach that cap. Rows past it are
not lost: they are still in the tool's `data` and CSV, which are never capped by this.

When a figure's labels are third-party text, `description`, `alt_text` and `data_table` are
**replaced** by `untrusted_description`, `untrusted_alt_text` and `untrusted_data_table`, never
returned beside them, and every cell is capped as above. The counts and the truncation note
are GeneFox's own text and stay under plain keys.

A figure can also be missing:

- `figure_unavailable`: no font, no output directory, nothing to draw, or a write failure.
- `figure_refused`: the engine's refusal sentence.

The server never draws an unlabelled figure.

With `inline_image: true`, a figure tool also returns an MCP content item
`{"type":"image","data":"<base64 PNG>","mimeType":"image/png"}` alongside the
existing text item. The cap is **1,048,576 PNG bytes** before base64 encoding, inclusive.
For a larger PNG, no image item is returned; `figure.inline_image_omitted` contains
`{"reason":"size_limit","bytes":N,"maximum_bytes":1048576}`. The PNG is still
written create-only and its file metadata is still returned. The argument defaults to
`false`; omitting it preserves the existing result bytes. This lets clients display figures
without access to the server's output directory. An unavailable or refused figure adds no
image content. The legacy `render_recipe` reports a render verdict and has no shared figure result.

With `html: true`, a tool also writes the screen's single-figure HTML document. That document's `<img alt>` is the figure's `alt_text`,
and after the figure it has a "Figure 1 data" table of the same rows, with the same 200-row
cap. Every string in it is HTML-escaped. If no figure was drawn, the result carries
`html_unavailable` instead; `tcga_case_expression` always answers `html_unavailable`, with the
reason, because its screen exports no HTML.

`csv: true` and `recipe: true` work the same way. They return `csv` or `recipe` (with
`path`, `bytes` and `sha256`), or `csv_unavailable` / `recipe_unavailable` with a reason.

## Parity tokens

The `figure.parity` and `html.parity` fields say how an output relates to what the app
exports:

| Token | Where | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app_export_identical` | `figure.parity` | The app screen's PNG export calls the same shared function with the same arguments. |
| `engine_only` | `figure.parity` | Drawn by the shared engine, but the screen has no PNG export to match; for example, the screen snapshots the view, or the figure was drawn with customized axes, which no screen draws yet. |
| `font_mismatch` | `figure.parity` | Replaces either value above when the figure font failed its SHA-256 pin. The glyph widths may differ from the app's. |
| `app_document_engine_png` | `html.parity` | The app's HTML document over the screen's title, subtitle, source and table, embedding the engine's PNG bytes. Apple re-encodes the same pixels. |
| `app_document_engine_figure` | `html.parity` | As above, but the screen snapshots this figure, so the app's own document embeds a snapshot where this one embeds the engine figure. |

The related fields are:

- **`figure.parity_screen`**: names the app screen the figure corresponds to.
- **`provenance.parity_screen`**: names the screen whose *numbers* the tool reproduces. The
  two can differ; for example, a Survival tab's numbers can come with an engine-drawn
  figure.
- **`parity_note`**: a sentence stating exactly where the output departs from the app,
  where there is something to say.
## Entitlements (GeneFox Pro)

The server **fails closed**. Pro tools are listed and callable only when the server grants the required capability. Hidden tools answer `-32602 Unknown tool`. No argument, flag, environment variable or file grants Pro access.

Pro tools: `batch_explorer_run`, `publication_studio_export`, `dataset_radar_check` and
`dose_response`. Without a live grant a Pro tool is not listed, and a direct call is refused
with `entitlement_required` before any file is opened. `genefox curated dose <view> <package-dir>`
runs `dose_response` from a terminal.

`account_status`
reports `linked: false`, `entitlement: "not_linked"`, `granted_capabilities: []` and
`cloud_ai: "off"`, with the caveat "Linking a GeneFox account to this server is not
available in this version."

`lab_collaboration_status`, `cloud_sync_status`, `cloud_sync_now` and `cloud_sync_store` are
free. They need a linked account, so in this version they report that none is linked.

## Account and cloud authority

Account linking, cloud retry and the dataset finder are **not available** in this build:

- **Disabled by default.** Each server context starts with an absent authority: no service,
  no profile, no evidence. No production tool creates a privileged publication, no MCP
  argument can supply a service, evidence or approval, and the authority is shut down at EOF.

- **One-use human approval.** The design requires a decision made in the human helper's own
  interface for linking and for each cloud request. An approval is bound to one exact
  request, host and authority generation, and is consumed when used.
- **Model-run commands are never human approval.** An agent running a terminal command, or a
  model setting a `force`-style flag, is not the human decision the design requires. No tool
  input can stand in for it.

Local conversations (`tcga_ask_open`, `geo_ask_open`, `ask_turn`, `ask_close`) use only a
host-owned local model and execute no analysis on their own. `local_model_status` reports
whether a local model is ready. On the Linux build it reports
`conversation: "unsupportedPlatform"` and `single_query: "unsupportedPlatform"`.

## Limits, deadlines and cancellation

| Limit | Value | Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Request line size | 4 MB (`maximumLineBytes`) | Refused before decoding: `-32700 "Request line exceeds 4 MB"`, id `null`. |
| JSON nesting depth | 32 levels, the envelope counting as 1 (`maximumNestingDepth`) | Refused before decoding: `-32700 "Request nesting exceeds 32 levels"`, id `null`. |
| Per-call deadline | 300 s by default; 900 s for the slow tools; 30 s for `ask_turn` (see the catalogue) | The call answers `timed_out` (retryable). The abandoned work may finish and fill the cache, so a retry is usually faster. |
| `--call-timeout` | 1–3600 s | Replaces every tool's deadline. |
| Concurrent calls (`--max-concurrent-calls`) | 1–64; default half the processors, 2 to 4; 16 more may queue | Beyond the queue: `rate_limited` (retryable, `details.source: genefox_server`), not run. Queued time counts against the deadline (`timed_out` with `details.queued: true`). |
| Early cancellations remembered | 256 | A `notifications/cancelled` that arrives before its request is remembered, and that request is then dropped. |
| GEO search cursors | 32 active searches, 15-minute idle expiry, 5,000 results per search | `cursor_capacity` (retryable), `cursor_expired`, `cursor_busy` (retryable), `pagination_limit`. |
| Local conversations | 2–8 sessions and 8–64 MB of snapshot memory in total, both measured from physical memory; 15-minute lifetime | `session_capacity`, `session_expired`, `session_busy` (retryable). |

The deadline timer is a Dispatch timer outside Swift's cooperative pool, so a saturated pool
cannot delay the `timed_out` verdict.

**Concurrency.** The read loop starts one task per request line **immediately**, so `ping`
and `tools/list` are never queued behind a slow analysis. Only `tools/call` passes the call
limiter: at most `--max-concurrent-calls` run at once and up to 16 more wait,
first come first served; a call beyond that answers `rate_limited` at once. A slot is held by
the work, not the answer, so a timed-out or cancelled call keeps it until its kernel returns.

## Error codes

### JSON-RPC errors

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `-32700` | Invalid JSON, a line over 4 MB, or nesting deeper than 32. Answered with id `null`. |
| `-32601` | Unsupported method. |
| `-32602` | `tools/call` named a tool that is not listed. For a legacy tool started without the flag, the message is `Tool not available: <name> is a legacy tool; start the server with --enable-legacy-tools`. |

### Tool errors

A tool error is a normal `tools/call` result with `isError: true`, whose text is
`{"error": {"code", "message", "retryable", "field"?, "details"?}}`. The codes used in this
tree are:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_argument` | An argument was refused (`field` names it), or an input file or report was unreadable. |
| `entitlement_required` | A GeneFox Pro argument (`field`) the context does not grant (`details.capability`); nothing was run. |
| `resource_unavailable` | The scientific resources, gene reference, or a report asset is missing. |
| `gene_not_found`, `ambiguous_gene` | The gene did not resolve, or resolved to more than one row (`details` lists the candidates). |
| `no_data`, `no_expression_data` | Nothing to analyse, or no expression matrix (GEO, Expression Atlas, supplementary files). |
| `not_runnable`, `unsupported_here`, `query_refused` | The analysis is refused with the app's sentence; the screen has no tool here; or the shared planner/validator refused the query. |
| `conflicting_loci`, `incomplete_family` (retryable), `upstream_partial_failure` (retryable) | Pan-cancer and pan-cancer survival assembly failures. |
| `upstream_unavailable` (retryable), `upstream_http` (retryable for 5xx), `rate_limited` (retryable, `retry_after`), `upstream_malformed`, `response_too_large` | Network and source failures. |
| `host_not_allowed` | The server reached a host outside the allowlist (`details.host`). |
| `seam_unavailable` | A platform seam was not installed. |
| `geo_search_failed`, `cursor_expired`, `cursor_busy`, `cursor_capacity`, `pagination_limit` | GEO search and pagination. |
| `session_capacity`, `session_expired`, `session_busy`, `session_limit`, `model_unavailable`, `invalid_model_response` | Local conversations. |
| `output_unavailable` | `report_export_pdf` has no usable output directory. |
| `timed_out` (retryable, `details.deadline_seconds`), `cancelled` | The deadline passed, or the call was cancelled. |
| `internal` | Anything else, with its message. |

Some file outputs fail without failing the call. They are reported beside the result as
`figure_unavailable`, `csv_unavailable`, `recipe_unavailable` or `html_unavailable`.

## Legacy tools

`--enable-legacy-tools` adds five tools that take a **local path or a URL**, which no other
tool does:

- **`report_export_pdf`**: a saved report to a PDF, written create-only to the output
  directory.
- **`report_export_html`**: a saved report to one self-contained HTML document, written
  create-only to the output directory.
- **`validate_recipe`**: the CLI's `validate` verdict.
- **`fetch_url`**: fetches through the installed transport. In `mcp` mode that is the
  allowlisted transport. `maximumBytes` must be between 1 and 100,663,296, the default is
  50 MB, and text over 100,000 bytes is returned as a preview.
- **`render_recipe`**: the CLI's `render`. An imported recipe reads only the store the server
  was started with (`--imported-store`); the model cannot choose a store, and a
  `storage_directory` argument is refused.

Without the flag they are neither listed nor callable (`-32602`).

A legacy tool reports a failure as `isError: true` with a plain-text sentence beginning
`error: `, not as the `{"error": {...}}` object described under [Tool errors](#tool-errors).
For example, `fetch_url` to a host outside the allowlist answers
`error: The GeneFox MCP server does not contact <host>: it reaches only the public-data hosts its tools need.`,
and the server logs `genefox mcp: host_not_allowed request host=<host>` to stderr.

## `list_coverage`

`list_coverage` takes no arguments. It returns one row per **free** app
operation: `row`, `operation`, `app_screen`, `mcp_tool` (or `null`), `status` and `note`. The
`status` is one of `available`, `partial`, `planned` or `not_available_headless`. The result
also has counts per status. On this build, `list_coverage` reported 54 available, 17
partial, 12 planned and 6 not available headlessly. A final row summarises Pro operations
without naming any; a context granted a Pro tool's capability also gets that tool's row after
it. Call `list_coverage` for the current state rather than relying on these
numbers.

Legacy local recipe paths are limited to the output directory, `--imported-store`, and
repeatable `--allow-root` directories (also `GENEFOX_MCP_ALLOWED_ROOTS`, separated by `:` on
POSIX or `;` on Windows). The server resolves links before testing containment, then opens
that canonical file without following replacement links. Validation and rendering consume
the bytes from that held handle, rather than reopening the model's path. Devices, sockets,
FIFOs, directories, and files above 64 MiB are refused with `local_path_*` codes; the byte
ceiling also applies if a file grows while it is read. `fetch_url` accepts only an allowed
public HTTP(S) URL and never turns a `file:` URL into a local read.
